title: Structure → properties
examples: What is the difference between giant and simple molecules?
Why do some substances melt at very high temperatures?
How does the structure affect the melting point?

explain.say: Today we explore how structure affects properties.

items: We look at two main types.

explain.say: Some substances form simple molecular structures.
These molecules are held together by weak forces.
Giant structures have strong bonds throughout.
Melting point relates to breaking these forces.
When heating, simple molecules break weak forces easily.

faq.q: Why do simple molecules have low melting points?
faq.a: They only have weak forces between the molecules that need to be overcome. This requires very little energy to break apart.
asks: What causes the low melting point?
Are the forces holding them together weak?

faq.q: What makes giant structures melt at high temperatures?
faq.a: Giant structures have strong covalent bonds throughout the entire lattice. Breaking these strong bonds requires a lot of energy.
asks: Why are the melting points so high?
Is it the bonds that are breaking?

faq.q: Does the strength of the bonds determine the melting point?
faq.a: Yes, the stronger the forces or bonds, the more energy is needed to change the state, resulting in a higher melting point.
asks: Does bond strength matter for melting?
What controls the melting point value?

faq.q: Are the forces in giant structures the same as the bonds?
faq.a: No, the bonds within a giant structure are strong covalent bonds. The forces between separate molecules are much weaker.
asks: Are the bonds covalent or intermolecular?
What is the difference between the two forces?

faq.q: Can you give an example of a giant structure?
faq.a: Silicon dioxide, which is found in sand, is a classic example of a giant structure.
asks: What is a common giant structure example?
Where can I find a giant structure?

facts: Simple molecular structures are held by weak intermolecular forces.
Giant molecular structures are held by strong covalent bonds throughout.
Melting point is related to the energy needed to overcome these forces.
Substances like diamond are examples of giant structures.

quiz.say: Which structure type has weak forces between particles?
quiz.why: Simple molecules are held together by relatively weak intermolecular forces.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because giant structures have strong bonds throughout.
wrong.1: Metals have delocalised electrons, which is a different type of bonding.
wrong.2: Ionic compounds form crystal lattices, not simple molecules.

quiz.say: A substance with a very high melting point likely has:
quiz.why: High melting points mean a lot of energy is needed, indicating strong bonds are broken.

wrong.0: Weak forces result in low melting points.
wrong.1: Simple molecules generally have low melting points.
wrong.2: While ionic bonds are strong, the concept applies to all strong covalent bonds.

quiz.say: If a substance melts easily, it probably has:
quiz.why: Melting easily means little energy is needed, suggesting weak forces are the main factor.

wrong.0: Strong covalent bonds require high energy to break.
wrong.1: Giant structures resist melting due to their strong bonding.
wrong.2: Ionic bonds are strong and require significant energy to break.
